name: MonarchAudioLevelMeter
title: AudioLevelMeter
summary: Shows how loud a microphone is, as rising segments or a thin bar, from a level the app measures.
whenToUse: In a call tile, a pre-call check or a recorder, to show that the microphone picks up sound.
whenNotToUse: For the progress of a recording or an upload use MonarchProgress. For a waveform over time, draw one from the samples.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAudioLevelMeter(level: Float, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchAudioLevelMeterVariant = MonarchAudioLevelMeterVariant.Segments, size: MonarchAudioLevelMeterSize = MonarchAudioLevelMeterSize.Md, segments: Int = 5, muted: Boolean = false, decorative: Boolean = false, label: String? = null, mutedLabel: String? = null)

options.name: level
options.description: The loudness, 0 to 1. Values outside are limited to that range; a value that is not finite is silence.

options.name: variant
options.description: Segments are rising bars the size of a word; Bar is one thin bar that fills the width.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm (12dp high) or Md (16dp). Segments only.

options.name: segments
options.description: The number of segments. At least one.

options.name: muted
options.description: The microphone is off: the meter is empty and reads "Muted".

states.name: silent
states.description: Every segment is a dot in the strong border color; the bar is an empty track.

states.name: sound
states.description: Segments up to the level are tall and in the success color; the bar is filled to the level.

states.name: muted
states.description: Empty, in the disabled color, and read as "Muted".

states.name: animations removed
states.description: The meter does not follow the level: it is full at or above a level of 0.08 and empty below.

appearance: Segments that are on use the success solid color and those that are off the strong border color; the bar's track is the muted background. A muted meter uses the disabled text color and the muted background. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web component can measure a MediaStream itself with the Web Audio API; on Android capturing audio needs the RECORD_AUDIO permission and an AudioRecord or a call SDK, which belong to the app, so the meter only takes a level, as on iOS. The level is a Float, as Compose progress values are. On the web a segment that is off keeps its height and changes color; here it is a dot, as on iOS. The web variants bars and bar are named Segments and Bar.
accessibility: The meter is one element named "Microphone level" (or label), with a progress range from 0 to 1 and a state description that is the level as a whole percentage in the user's locale, or "Muted".
It is not a live region, so TalkBack does not read every change of the level.
When animations are removed the meter shows only whether there is sound; the spoken value is still the real level.
Segments that are on are tall and segments that are off are dots, so the level does not depend on color.
decorative hides it when the same information is given elsewhere.
It is not interactive and has no touch target.
edgeCases: A level that is not finite is treated as silence.
A segment count below one draws one segment.
The level changes without animation; pass a smoothed level for a calmer meter.
Segments rise towards the end and the bar fills from the start in both layout directions; the mirroring is done when drawing and is not covered by a pixel test.

parityExceptions.reason: The web example is an animated meter with no text, tone or button, so there is no scenario to pin.
parityExceptions.convention: Both native components keep their own examples.
